samples.summary: Sanitizer accepts a zero-column table: `cols` can be 0, producing a table block with empty rows and empty `columnWidths`
samples.evidence: `sanitizeTableData` returns a table whenever at least one row object with a `cells` array survives. A payload like `{rows:[{cells:[]}]}` yields `cols = Math.max(...[0]) = 0`, so the padding loop (274) does nothing, the width loop (281) never runs (`columnWidths = []`, and the `1 / cols === Infinity` default is dead only by luck), and `normalizeTableMerges` no-ops on `numCols === 0`. `sanitizeBlock` then returns a `type: 'table'` block with a degenerate grid, which is inserted into the document (and into the shared CRDT). Downstream code assumes a rectangle with at least one cell: `insertBlocks` cannot place the caret (`rows[0]?.cells[0]?.blocks[0]` is undefined), `selection.ts:448` computes `colIndex: -1`, and the arrow-key paths (`text-editor.ts:2510`) index `cells[0]` on an empty row. A `cols >= 1` (or reject) guard is missing. Secondary: `Math.max(...rows.map(...))` spreads one argument per row, so a payload with >~100k rows throws RangeError — swallowed by the outer try/catch, turning the paste into a silent no-op.

samples.summary: The new empty-list-item split workaround in `insertBlocks` is bypassed by `insertPlainText`, which still hits `Doc.splitBlock`'s short-circuit
samples.evidence: `insertBlocks` now guards against `Doc.splitBlock` returning the *same* block id for an empty list item (`splitExitsList`, line 3619). `insertPlainText` (line 3540) calls the same `docSplitBlock` with no such guard: with the caret on an empty list item, the split exits the list and returns `pos.blockId`, so `cursor.moveTo({blockId: newBlockId})` stays put and the next line's text is appended to the same block instead of a new one (paste of `"\nfoo"` into an empty bullet yields one block, not two). Same short-circuit, same class of bug, unguarded call site.

samples.summary: Heading-memory provenance rule is inconsistent between typing and pasting into an emptied bulleted heading
samples.evidence: `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` is applied to a single-block paste (`pastedTextLen > 0 && mergeDropsHeadingMemory(block)`), so pasting "body text" into an empty bulleted heading drops the remembered level. Typing the same characters goes through `Doc.insertText`/`store.insertText`, which never consults the predicate, so the level survives and un-listing promotes the newly typed text to a heading. Two identical end states differ in whether the memory survives; one of the two behaviours is wrong (probably the paste one, since an emptied heading in Google Docs stays a heading when retyped).

samples.summary: `applyMergeBlocks` drops the destination's stale memory but never adopts the incoming block's memory, losing heading provenance in the mirror case
samples.evidence: `applyMergeBlocks` deletes `merged.headingLevel` when the destination list item holds no text, but ignores `nextBlock.headingLevel`. Merging an empty plain bullet with a following bulleted heading (Backspace at the start of the heading bullet) produces a block whose whole text *was* a heading, with no memory — the symmetric case that `splitMovesHeadingMemory` deliberately handles for splits (memory follows the text). The two helpers therefore disagree on the same provenance rule, and a split-then-merge round trip loses the heading.

samples.summary: Numeric fields are shape-checked but never range-checked, so a payload can inject absurd geometry through the new sanitizer
samples.evidence: `asNumber` only requires `typeof === 'number' && Number.isFinite`. `listLevel` and `headingLevel` are clamped, but `columnWidths` entries (281), `padding`, `letterSpacing`, `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `marginLeft`, and every `ImageData` numeric (`width`, `height`, crops, `rotation`) accept negatives and values like `1e12`. A pasted `columnWidths: [-5]` or `fontSize: 1e9` reaches `computeTableLayout` / the canvas measurer directly, producing negative-width columns or an effectively unbounded layout pass. Since the stated purpose of this rewrite is to constrain untrusted payload values, the clamping is half-applied.

samples.summary: New `headingLevel` removals use the subtree-wide `removeStyleByPath(path, path+1)` pattern the file's own `removeNodeStyle` helper exists to avoid
samples.evidence: The doc comment on `removeNodeStyle` (lines 260-274) states explicitly that `removeStyleByPath(path, path+1, …)` is not node-scoped — it applies the removal to every element node in the subtree — and that Yorkie's index-range `removeStyle` must be used instead. The two new removals (splitBlock 2067, mergeBlock 2253) use exactly the forbidden pattern. It is harmless today only because split/merge reject `table` blocks so the subtree holds only inline nodes (which never carry `headingLevel`); it becomes a real over-removal the moment a block type can nest blocks. Use `removeNodeStyle(tree, blockPath, ['headingLevel'])`.

finding.summary: Clipboard sanitizer drops `colSpan: 0` covered-cell markers, breaking merged tables on internal paste
finding.evidence:
`sanitizeCell` only keeps a span when it is `> 1`:
```
if (colSpan !== undefined && colSpan > 1) cell.colSpan = Math.trunc(colSpan);
```
But `colSpan: 0` is the *covered-cell marker* the layout relies on — `normalizeTableMerges` (model/types.ts:592) writes `cell.colSpan = 0` for every cell an anchor covers (including rowSpan coverage), and `computeTableLayout` (view/table-layout.ts:158-164) skips a cell only when `colSpan === 0`. Before this change the payload's cells were passed through verbatim, so the markers survived a copy/paste.

The cell-range paste path self-heals (`pasteTableCells` calls `normalizeTableMerges`, text-editor.ts:3708/3740), but the whole-table-block paste path does **not**: `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts:3565-3584) inserts `cloneBlockWithFreshIds(blocks[0])` with no normalization. So copying a table that contains merged cells and pasting it back produces a table whose merges are gone — the previously covered cells render as real cells with their own width, and any anchor keeps `colSpan > 1`, violating the invariant the layout documents it trusts.

verdict.reason: The quoted `sanitizeCell` line is real (clipboard.ts:239 keeps only spans > 1), but the claimed effect is prevented in the same function chain: `sanitizeTableData` pads rows into a rectangle (clipboard.ts:270-275) and then calls `normalizeTableMerges(table)` (clipboard.ts:293, imported at clipboard.ts:8), which re-derives every covered cell's `colSpan = 0` from the surviving anchors' preserved colSpan/rowSpan (types.ts:600-633, marker written at types.ts:608, rowSpan coverage at types.ts:628-633) and clamps out-of-grid spans (types.ts:624-627). Since every pasted table block is produced through `sanitizeBlock` -> `sanitizeTableData` (clipboard.ts:313-318), the whole-table-block path receives an already-normalized TableData, so `insertBlocks` not normalizing is harmless; the cell-range path normalizes as well (text-editor.ts:3712, 3744). The reviewer's evidence omitted the normalization call that the finding depends on being absent.

finding.summary: `columnWidths` fallback of `100` is in the wrong unit — column widths are ratios, not pixels
finding.evidence:
`for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 100);`

`TableData.columnWidths` holds *fractions*: `createTableBlock` fills `Array(cols).fill(1 / cols)` (model/types.ts:542), the DOCX importer divides by `totalWidth` (import/docx-importer.ts:277), and the layout does `columnWidths.map(ratio => ratio * contentWidth)` (view/table-layout.ts:140). A fallback of `100` therefore yields a column 100× the content width whenever an entry is missing or non-numeric (a truncated or hostile payload, or a row that has more cells than the payload has widths). The correct default is `1 / cols`.

verdict.reason: The finding's quoted evidence does not exist. clipboard.ts:281 already reads `columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 1 / cols)` — the fallback is the even-share fraction, i.e. the exact correction the finding asks for, and lines 278-280 document that widths are fractions and must not default to 100. A grep for `?? 100` across packages/docs/src returns no matches, so no pixel-unit fallback exists anywhere on this path. The underlying invariant (types.ts:558 fills 1/cols; table-layout.ts:140 multiplies ratio * contentWidth) is real but already respected by the sanitizer.
